page: Microsoft Azure D2_v4 is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyper-threading. Hardware features include 35 MB of shared L3 cache, AVX-512 vector extensions, and AVX-512 VNNI support. Memory allocation stands at 8.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This VM tier does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network-attached storage for system disks and persistence.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded capabilities but constrained multi-core throughput due to the single physical core allocation. In synthetic evaluation, stress-ng single-core performance reached 1427.09 and Geekbench single-core reached 1218.0, placing both within the middle 50% performance bracket. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into the lower tiers, registering a multi-core Geekbench score of 1466.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2218.71. Uncached memory throughput measures 12.96 GB/sec for reads and 10.78 GB/sec for writes, which restricts heavy memory-bound data shuffling.

The qualitative cost profile makes the D2_v4 an economical option for workloads that do not demand parallel processing or ephemeral local disk speed. Because storage relies fully on remote network volumes, I/O intensive transactional operations face latency and throughput constraints compared to instances equipped with local NVMe. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for low-traffic web applications, lightweight background worker services, small staging environments, and basic microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D2_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical Intel Xeon 8272CL core running at 2.6 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, the instance relies entirely on remote Azure managed disks for storage needs. Performance benchmarks reflect moderate single-threaded compute, scoring 1218.0 on Geekbench single-core, but multi-threaded processing and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the single-core topology. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. With its balanced 1:4 processor-to-memory configuration and low operational footprint, the D2_v4 provides an efficient foundation for lightweight server tasks, microservices, small development environments, and low-traffic web application hosting.
